Assistant:
chosen: A compiled language converts your source code into machine code all at once before the program runs — the compiler reads your code, checks it for errors, and produces an executable file. C and C++ are examples. An interpreted language runs your code line by line through an interpreter at the time of execution, so there is no separate compilation step. Python and JavaScript are examples. Compiled languages are generally faster at runtime, while interpreted languages are often easier to develop and debug interactively.
